page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.large is an entry-tier general purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor clocked at 2.55 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instruction sets, while newer AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Cache distribution includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-thread capability contrasted with limited multi-core throughput due to its 2 vCPU ceiling. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached 2683.19 points, falling into the top quartile. However, the multi-core stress-ng metric reached 2690.88, remaining in the lower quartile alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 1836.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 1957.0. Memory throughput registered at 31.79 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 16.81 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding a PassMark memory score of 1389.57. Redis operations achieved 2.02 million SET requests per second, and static web serving throughput reached 2.45 GB/sec.

The ecs.g7a.large does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is capped at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Given its modest core count and entry-level throughput, this server delivers proportional cost efficiency for non-parallelized execution paths. The hardware profile is appropriate for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch tasks, small staging environments, text processing, and auxiliary microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.large is a general-purpose virtual instance featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz with 1 physical core and 2 dedicated vCPUs. It includes 8.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, a 1 Gbps baseline network interface, and no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top quartile on single-core stress-ng tests at 2683.19 points, while multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth remain in the lower quartiles due to the 2-vCPU configuration. Cryptographic support includes AES and SHA-NI extensions, but AVX-512 is unsupported. With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, ecs.g7a.large is suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, modest text and data processing tasks, staging environments, and single-threaded background jobs that do not require heavy concurrent compute.
